MANCHESTER SCHOOL DISTRICT SAU #37 
SPECIAL COMMITTEE ON ATHLETICS 
 
October 14, 2026 9:30 a.m.  
 
9:00 a.m. –  Non-Meeting with Legal Counsel – exempt from public disclosure under the 
provisions of RSA 91-A:2, I (b) consultation with legal counsel. 
 
1. Chairwoman Stewart called the meeting to order at 9:34 a.m. 
 
2. The Clerk called the roll.  
 
Present:  Committee Members Cindy Stewart, Jim O'Connell, and Sam Garrity. 
Absent:  Committee Member Sean Parr. 
 
Chair Stewart acknowledged the recent passing of Committee Member Parr's mother and extended 
condolences, thoughts, and well wishes to him and his family. 
 
 
3. Public Forum 
 
There were no individuals signed up to speak. 
 
6. Approval of the Minutes of the following meetings: September 9, 2026. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Garrity, duly seconded by Committee Member O’Connell, it was 
moved to approve the minutes of the September 9, 2026, meeting of the Special Committee on Athletics.  
All were in favor and the motion passed.  
 
7. PRESENTATIONS  
 
There were no presentations at this meeting. 
 
 
8. Spectator Code of Conduct – by Dr. Kelly Espinola, Assistant Superintendent  
 
Dr. Espinola presented the proposed Manchester School District Athletics Spectator Code of Conduct, 
developed in response to increasing concerns regarding spectator behavior at athletic events, including 
interactions with coaches, officials, student-athletes, and opposing teams.  She explained that athletic 
events are an extension of the school environment and that spectators are expected to demonstrate the 
same standards of respect, appropriate behavior, and safety that are required within District schools. The
October 14, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 2 of 8 
 
proposed code establishes expectations for supporting student-athletes, respecting coaches and officials, 
using appropriate language, remaining within designated spectator areas, and demonstrating respectful 
conduct both in person and online. 
 
The code also addresses appropriate methods for communicating concerns or disagreements and 
establishes potential consequences for inappropriate or unsafe behavior, including removal from events 
or restrictions on future attendance. 
 
An infographic was presented outlining these expectations. Upon approval by the full Board, the District 
intends to print and display the infographic at athletic fields and gymnasiums. 
 
On motion of Committee Member O'Connell, duly seconded by Committee Member Garrity, it was 
moved to approve the Athletics Spectator Code of Conduct and forward the item to the full Board of 
School Committee for approval. 
 
During discussion, Chair Stewart expressed support for displaying the code at athletic facilities and 
suggested including it within the athletic registration portal, potentially with a parent or guardian 
acknowledgment.  Additional discussion focused on communicating the code through multiple channels, 
including the District website, registration materials, beginning-of-season communications, and postings 
at athletic events.  The Administration indicated that a parent/student-athlete code of conduct had 
already been incorporated into the fall registration process and that the proposed spectator infographic 
could also be uploaded to the registration portal. 
 
Committee Member O'Connell raised concerns regarding additional acknowledgment requirements, 
questioning their effectiveness and the possibility of creating unnecessary barriers for families.   The 
Administration agreed that distributing the expectations through existing communication methods would 
provide sufficient notice without requiring an additional signature. 
 
The Committee also discussed the importance of communicating expectations and potential 
consequences to spectators and suggested that similar messaging could eventually extend to other 
extracurricular activities, including performing arts events.
October 14, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 3 of 8 
 
Following discussion, the Committee agreed to proceed with the proposed code and utilize multiple 
methods of communication to ensure that spectator expectations are widely available. 
 
All were in favor and the motion passed. 
 
 
9. Game Personnel Administration for Manchester School District Elementary    
School Basketball – by Christine Telge, Director of Athletics; Jordan D’Onofrio,  
Assistant Director of Athletics; and, Dr. Kelly Espinola, Assistant Superintendent   
 
Mrs. Telge and Mr. D’Onofrio presented the results of a Request for Proposals (RFP) for game 
personnel administration for the Manchester School District Elementary School Basketball League. 
In accordance with District procurement procedures, the RFP was advertised in the New Hampshire 
Union Leader, posted on the District website, and distributed directly to potential vendors.  One 
proposal was received. Following review in conjunction with the Business Office, the Athletic 
Department recommended awarding the contract to Manchester Youth Sports in the amount of $24,500, 
utilizing budgeted funds. 
 
It was explained that the contract covers game officials, scorekeepers, and timekeepers at both 
basketball locations throughout the Saturday league schedule. 
 
In response to questions from Committee Member O'Connell, the Administration clarified that the 
Athletics Department separately funds coaching stipends, additional personnel, equipment, uniforms, 
and associated facility expenses. The proposed contract is specifically for game personnel administration 
and does not transfer responsibility for operating the league to the vendor. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Garrity, duly seconded by Committee Member O’Connell, it was 
moved to approve awarding the bid for game personnel administration for the Manchester School 
District Elementary School Basketball League to Manchester Youth Sports in the amount of $24,500 and 
forward the item to the full Board of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the motion 
passed.
October 14, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 4 of 8 
 
 
10. Upcoming Items: 
 
1. Alumni Athletes and Identification of Community Partners 
 
Chair Stewart discussed the continued importance of engaging former Manchester student-athletes and 
identifying additional community partnerships to support District athletic programs.  She recognized the 
recent partnership with Dr. Nick Vailas and the Safe Sports Network, which provided free athletic 
physical examinations to approximately 40 students. She also expressed appreciation for the Safe Sports 
Network's continued provision of athletic trainers at District events at no cost. 
 
Chair Stewart additionally recognized Dr. George Jumpp, a Memorial High School alumnus and local 
chiropractor, for his commitment to providing Manchester School District student-athletes with two 
complimentary visits annually.   
 
The Committee agreed to retain alumni athlete engagement and community partnership development as 
upcoming agenda items to encourage further collaboration and opportunities for students. 
 
 
11. NEW BUSINESS  
 
1. Policy Students 539: Student Insurance 
Attorney Upton presented a recommendation to repeal Policy Students 539, Student Insurance, 
explaining that the insurance referenced within the policy is no longer available. 
 
On motion of Committee Member O’Connell, duly seconded by Committee Member Garrity, it was 
moved to approve the repealing of Policy Students 539: Student Insurance and forward the 
recommendation to the full Board of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the motion 
passed. 
 
2. Policy Students 542:  Physical Examinations 
 
Attorney Upton presented proposed amendments to Policy Students 542, Physical Examinations, 
recommending that the required frequency of physical examinations for participation in athletics be 
changed from annually to at least once every two calendar years.  The proposed change was based on
October 14, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 5 of 8 
 
consultation with medical professionals and was intended to reduce potential barriers to student 
participation in athletics. 
 
Questions and comments included: 
1. Committee Member O'Connell expressed concern regarding existing language requiring the 
District to schedule free physical examinations. He suggested revising the language to maintain 
access for students who need assistance while avoiding an unnecessarily broad obligation for the 
District to provide physical examinations to all student-athletes. 
2. The Committee discussed the significant number of students who may have difficulty accessing 
physical examinations and emphasized the importance of maintaining opportunities for those 
students to obtain the examinations necessary for athletic participation. 
3. The Committee agreed to amend the policy by removing the existing language regarding 
scheduled physical examinations and replacing it with:  "Free physical examinations will be 
made available when needed." 
4. The Committee also agreed to eliminate the subsequent sentence regarding students who miss 
scheduled physical examinations, as it would no longer be necessary under the revised language. 
 
On motion of Committee Member O’Connell, duly seconded by Committee Member Garrity, it was 
moved to approve the amendments to Students 542:  Physical Examinations and forward the 
recommendation to the full Board of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the motion 
passed. 
 
 
3. Policy Students 521: Extracurricular Activities 
 
Attorney Upton presented proposed amendments to Policy Students 521, Extracurricular Activities, 
including changes related to physical examination requirements. 
 
Committee Member O'Connell identified several additional areas of the policy requiring clarification or 
revision.  Following discussion, the Committee agreed to the following amendments:
October 14, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 6 of 8 
 
1. Reference to High Schools: Remove the specific reference to "high school" within the 
introductory language to ensure the policy applies appropriately to students at all applicable 
grade levels. The revised language will reference opportunities that "the school has to offer." 
2. Social Promotion: Delete the sentence referencing students who are "socially promoted" to 
ninth grade being placed on academic probation. Committee members discussed the outdated 
nature of the terminology and the importance of considering students' individual academic 
circumstances. 
3. Minimum Course Enrollment: Delete the sentence requiring students to be enrolled in a 
minimum of four courses during a grading period. Discussion addressed changes in educational 
opportunities, including charter schools, homeschooling, alternative education, and Education 
Freedom Account participation. 
 
The Administration clarified that applicable New Hampshire Interscholastic Athletic Association 
(NHIAA) eligibility requirements would continue to govern athletic participation regardless of whether 
the specific four-course requirement appeared in District policy.  The Athletic Department also 
explained that it had implemented an academic eligibility verification process for students attending 
nontraditional educational programs. The process requires verification from an appropriate academic 
representative, such as a parent, guardian, principal, dean, or educational advisor, to document 
compliance with applicable athletic eligibility requirements. 
 
The Committee agreed that existing policy language requiring compliance with NHIAA rules and 
regulations sufficiently addressed this matter without separately restating the four-course requirement. 
 
On motion of Committee Member O’Connell, duly seconded by Committee Member Garrity, it was 
moved to approve the amendments to Students 521: Extracurricular Activities and forward the 
recommendation to the full Board of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the motion 
passed. 
 
Chair Stewart clarified that Policies Students 539, 542, and 521 would be forwarded to the full Board of 
School Committee for consideration, with the recommended repeal and amendments reflected 
accordingly.
October 14, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 7 of 8 
 
The Administration indicated that winter athletic registration was scheduled to open that day, with the 
intention of having the proposed policy revisions addressed before the beginning of winter athletic 
tryouts. 
 
ADDITIONAL NEW BUSINESS 
 
City of Manchester Parks and Recreation — Use of School Facilities and Elementary Athletics 
Committee Member O'Connell raised the topic of the City of Manchester Parks and Recreation 
Department's use of District school facilities, referencing a previously approved arrangement intended to 
provide additional recreational opportunities for elementary-aged students.  He requested that the 
Administration provide an update to the Committee on Finance regarding the arrangement and its 
effectiveness, noting that the matter was expected to return for consideration in November. 
Administration indicated that the arrangement had been successful. 
 
Discussion followed regarding potential opportunities for greater collaboration between the District and 
the City's recreation programs, including the possibility of the City assuming a larger role in managing 
elementary athletic programs. 
 
Committee Member O'Connell noted that municipalities such as Concord and Nashua operate 
elementary athletic programs through their municipal recreation departments, allowing school district 
athletic departments to concentrate resources on middle and high school athletics. 
 
The Committee discussed the potential benefits of establishing stronger feeder programs for younger 
students and expanding athletic participation opportunities throughout Manchester.  The Administration 
noted that increased facility use would also require consideration of custodial services and cleaning 
expenses. The District's current Aramark contract does not fully account for additional recreational 
programming, and existing custodial resources are limited by budget constraints. 
 
The discussion included the importance of addressing responsibility for facility cleaning and associated 
costs as part of any future expansion of municipal recreational programming.  The Athletic Department 
indicated that the District's elementary basketball program costs approximately $50,000 annually.
October 14, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 8 of 8 
 
Committee members expressed interest in continued discussion regarding coordination with the City and 
the potential for expanding elementary athletic opportunities while considering staffing, facilities, and 
financial implications. 
 
No formal action was taken. 
 
 
ADJOURNMENT 
 
12. If there is no further business, a motion is in order to adjourn.  
 
On motion of Committee Member Garrity, duly seconded by Committee Member O’Connell, it was 
moved to adjourn.  All were in favor, meeting adjourned at 10:11 a.m.

Clerk of Committee
